messages:
sam: Heads up — we had a customer hit the primary model QPS cap and traffic stalled for ~90s. Thinking we should add automatic model-variant fallback based on capacity signals (not just latency). :thinking:
maya: We need to be careful — premium customers should not automatically drop to lower-quality variants unless they opted in or it's allowed by tier.
jia: Agreed. Also need console visibility + an opt-out toggle per-customer.
alejandro: From infra side, runtime can emit saturation signals (available_workers=0, queue_len>1000) and a reason code 'SATURATED'. Router can interpret that to trigger fallback. We already have an 'overloaded' signal from autoscaler, reuseable.
maya: Also boundaries: don't let premium bleed into shared pools. Fallback should respect routing policy: allowed_variants and max_cost_budget.
sam: Proposed policy model: ordered variant list per route (primary, fallback-1, fallback-2) + per-variant conditions (saturation_threshold, allowed_tiers, cost_penalty). Router only moves to next variant on explicit saturation or hard reject, and does a gradual shift to avoid thundering herd.
priya: How to prevent flash migration? If everyone flips to variant B simultaneously, it could cascade.
sam: Plan: gradual rollout percentage when fallback triggers (e.g., 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 30s), per-customer cooldown windows, and per-variant admission control. Also add a short-lived queue to smooth spikes.
jia: UI/telemetry: console should show "fallback active" with live rate, p95 latency delta, and ability to force-disable fallback for a customer. Also emit events: variant_transition, fallback_triggered, fallback_cleared.
alejandro: API change: router.proto add enum FallbackReason { NONE, SATURATED, REJECTED, DEGRADED } and include ordered_variant_ids in RouteDecision. Telemetry schema update for variant_transition.
maya: UX ask: show which variant is currently serving and a small explanation (e.g., "primary saturated: 3 workers available"). Allow admins to set "fallback_mode: gradual|immediate|disabled" per route.
priya: Dev question: where to keep the policy config? Console + versioned policy stored in control plane (route config). Runtime caches for fast lookup.
sam: Example policy snippet (rough):
```yaml
route: /chat/gen
variants:
  - id: redwood-v1
    allowed_tiers: [free, standard, premium]
    saturation_threshold: 0.85
  - id: redwood-v1-quant
    allowed_tiers: [standard, premium]
    cost_penalty: 0.6
    saturation_threshold: 0.9
  - id: redwood-mini
    allowed_tiers: [free]
fallback_mode: gradual
max_burst_fallback: 0.1 # percent of traffic to move immediately
```
alejandro: Ops concerns: need clear metrics to know when fallback made things worse (quality regressions). Hook into existing evals and attach automated rollback if quality drop > X% over baseline.
maya: Also need quota enforcement: fallback shouldn't let a tenant exceed their reserved capacity silently. If premium falls back to shared, we need billing/alerting labels.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for "router/fallback-v1" to 5% of traffic in us-east-1 at 1801234575.
priya: I'll own router changes and admission control. Sam, can you draft the RFC for policy semantics and console UX? Jia can you add telemetry events and eval harness updates?
sam: Yup — I'll draft RFC today and ping design for console mocks. Target: canary deploy next week, full rollout after 2-week canary/metrics window. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: rollout status: canary healthy (5% -> steady).
maya: Great. Please add a short-runbook for oncall describing how to disable fallback if it's causing regressions.
priya: Will do.
